title: Buddhism, Jainism and the Mahajanapadas

cards.h: A new age of thought and states
cards.b: About 600 BCE the Ganga plains saw the second urbanisation, new kingdoms and religions that questioned ritual. This sets the stage for the Mauryas.

Rituals and sacrifices were costly; Brahmin dominance and the varna order irked Kshatriyas and Vaishyas. Iron ploughs and trade made merchants rich; they wanted respect. Cities and coins grew. Reformers offered simple, ethical paths in local languages.

Siddhartha Gautama (c. 563 to 483 BCE, Lumbini); enlightenment at Bodh Gaya; first sermon at Sarnath (Dharmachakra Pravartana); died at Kushinagar. Four Noble Truths: suffering, its cause (craving), its end (nirvana), the Eightfold Path. Middle Path, anatta, karma. The Sangha admitted women (Mahaprajapati Gotami). Councils: Rajagriha (483 BCE), Vaishali (383 BCE), Pataliputra (Ashoka, c. 250 BCE), Kashmir (Kanishka). Sects: Theravada, Mahayana (Nagarjuna), Vajrayana. Texts: Tripitaka in Pali.

Vardhamana Mahavira, the 24th Tirthankara (c. 540 to 468 BCE, Vaishali). Predecessor Parshvanatha. Five vows (ahimsa, satya, asteya, aparigraha, brahmacharya); three jewels (right faith, knowledge, conduct); anekantavada (many-sidedness of truth). Split into Digambara (Bhadrabahu) and Svetambara (Sthulabhadra) after famine around 300 BCE; the council at Pataliputra and Vallabhi (512 CE). Patrons: Bimbisara, Ajatashatru, Chandragupta Maurya, Kharavela of Kalinga, Chalukyas.

Anguttara Nikaya lists 16 (Kashi, Kosala, Anga, Magadha, Vajji, Malla, Chedi, Vatsa, Kuru, Panchala, Machchha, Surasena, Assaka, Avanti, Gandhara, Kamboja). Most were monarchies; some were gana-sanghas (republics) such as the Vajji (Vaishali) and Malla. Capitals: Rajagriha, Shravasti, Ujjain, Kaushambi. Coins: punch-marked silver karshapana. Fortified cities.

Reasons: fertile plains, nearby iron mines, rivers for trade, elephants, strong rulers. Haryanka: Bimbisara (c. 544 to 492 BCE; Anga annexed; marriages), Ajatashatru (Vajji war; first Council), Udayin (Pataliputra). Shishunaga dynasty. Nanda dynasty: Mahapadma Nanda, “sole sovereign” (c. 345 BCE), large army; their wealth. Alexander invaded in 326 BCE (battle of the Hydaspes against Porus) and his army refused to go further.

Second urbanisation: Rajagriha, Vaishali, Kaushambi, Ujjain. Guilds (shrenis), the setthi (merchant), trade routes (Uttarapatha). Gahapati landholders. Social mobility for merchants. Iron tools, NBPW pottery (Northern Black Polished Ware), coins. Women of the Sangha and Jaina nuns show new paths.

cards.h: Why did Buddhism decline in India?
cards.b: Reasons offered: revival of Brahmanism (Shankara, bhakti), Buddhist splits and monastic wealth, loss of royal patronage, invasions (Huns, Turks) and destruction of monasteries (Nalanda, c. 1200). Scholars such as D. N. Jha and Romila Thapar caution against single causes; Buddhism spread widely abroad. B. R. Ambedkar wrote on Buddha and his Dhamma (1957) and on the reasons for decline.

The Ashoka Chakra on the flag and the lion capital are Buddhist symbols. Ambedkar’s conversion (14 October 1956, Nagpur) shaped Dalit politics. Buddhist circuit tourism (Bodh Gaya, Sarnath, Kushinagar; Kushinagar airport 2021), the Nalanda University revival (2010 Act, new campus in 2024), and the Jain concept of aparigraha in sustainability debates link the past to now.
